character: Glamour, luxury, Michelin stars, designer shopping — but also genuinely excellent skiing in the world's largest linked domain.
description: Courchevel is not one resort but four villages, each at a different altitude with a different personality. The collective name covers 1850 (luxury, designer boutiques, Michelin stars), 1650/Moriond (family-friendly, more relaxed), 1550/Village (quiet, traditional, lower prices), and 1300/Le Praz (oldest, most authentic). The higher you go, the more prestigious — and expensive — it gets.

stats.michelin_stars: 11 in Les 3 Vallées, highest concentration in Courchevel 1850

villages.name: Courchevel 1850
villages.character: The flagship. Designer boutiques (Chanel, LV, Prada, Valentino, Cartier, Saint Laurent), 5-star hotels (Aman Le Mélézin, Cheval Blanc, L'Apogée), 3 Michelin-starred restaurants, private jet airport (Altiport). Ultra-luxury, glamorous, and expensive — but the ski-in/ski-out access and central location are genuinely excellent.
villages.architecture: Mix of luxury chalets and 1970s purpose-built blocks — bling covers the concrete
villages.shopping: Chanel, Valentino, Louis Vuitton, Prada, Cartier, Saint Laurent, Dior — rivals Paris boutiques. Forum Centre has supermarket, pharmacy, sports shops.

michelin: Baumanière 1850 — ★★ Michelin, Chef Thomas Prod'homme, Alpine-Provencal, €€€€
Le Sarkara — ★★ Michelin, Chef Sébastien Vauxion, haute vegetarian pâtisserie, €€€€
signature: Le Tremplin — iconic slope-side bar/restaurant at piste base, see-and-be-seen
La Cave des Creux — piste-side, run by local ski instructors, great terrace with Mont Blanc view

villages.apres: La Folie Douce (iconic afternoon party), Les Caves (nightclub), Le Tremplin (slope-side), Bar des Pistes (Aman), piano bars

villages.name: Courchevel 1650 (Moriond)
villages.character: Family-friendly, more relaxed, less expensive than 1850. Hosts the Aquamotion water park — a major draw for families with children.
attractions: Aquamotion — indoor/outdoor water park with heated pools, slides, spa, fitness
villages.dining: Good selection of mid-range restaurants, less formal than 1850

villages.name: Courchevel 1550 (Village)
villages.character: The original hamlet of Courchevel. Quieter, more traditional, lower prices. Good for those who want Courchevel access without the 1850 price tag.

villages.name: Courchevel 1300 (Le Praz)
villages.character: The oldest and most authentic of the Courchevel villages. Traditional Savoyard architecture, quiet, charming. Home to Le Farçon (★ Michelin) and La Tania next door.
villages.dining: Le Farçon — ★ Michelin, rustic-chic, ski-in/ski-out accessible from slopes
villages.note: Most authentic architecture in the Courchevel valley

spas_and_wellness: Aman Le Mélézin Spa — 767 sqm over 2 floors, hammam, cold plunge pool, 14m indoor lap pool, yoga studio, TRX fitness, 5 treatment rooms, Thai massage suite, Himalayan salt scrub, Japanese tea ceremony
Cheval Blanc Spa — Guerlain beauty treatments, hammam, sauna, Russian banya, outdoor jacuzzi
Spa des Neiges by Clarins — facials, massages, makeup
Aquamotion — water park with indoor/outdoor heated pools, slides, spa (1650)
L'Apogée Spa — Oxygene spa, indoor pool, treatment rooms
non_ski_activities.shopping: Chanel, Valentino, Louis Vuitton, Prada, Cartier, Saint Laurent, Dior, plus Forum Centre with supermarket, pharmacy, sports equipment, art galleries
non_ski_activities.ice_skating: Olympic-standard indoor ice rink (built for 1992 Albertville Games) at Forum Centre, skate rental on site
non_ski_activities.sledging: 2 km night-lit sledging run from 1850 (near Forum) to 1550 (Village), open day and night, 300m vertical drop
non_ski_activities.swimming: Aquamotion water park + indoor pools at several 5-star hotels
non_ski_activities.cinema: Cinema in 1850, some screenings in English with subtitles
non_ski_activities.bowling: Bowling 3000 — 6 lanes, child-friendly, at Forum Centre
non_ski_activities.climbing: Indoor climbing wall at Forum Centre + ice climbing on 18m artificial wall + guided ice climbing on natural waterfalls
non_ski_activities.paragliding: Tandem paragliding flights from Saulire summit (2,700m) — €€€
non_ski_activities.scenic_flights: Helicopter tours from Altiport (private jet airport), hot air balloon rides
non_ski_activities.horse_drawn: Horse-drawn sleigh rides through forest trails
non_ski_activities.dog_sledding: Multiple providers — half-day and full-day excursions with huskies
non_ski_activities.snowshoeing: Marked trails through forests and Vanoise National Park
non_ski_activities.fat_biking: Fat bike hire and guided rides on snow trails
non_ski_activities.snowmobiling: Guided snowmobile excursions after lift closure
non_ski_activities.fitness: Gym and fitness centre at Forum + yoga classes at multiple venues
non_ski_activities.events: Winter Legacy by Alexis Pinturault, weekly street market, concerts, piano bars

traditional: La Cave des Creux — piste-side, by local ski instructors Boris and Florian Glise
Le Tremplin — iconic slope-side see-and-be-seen spot
La Grand'table — traditional Savoyard, excellent tartiflette
Le Bistrot du Praz — relaxed, good value, Le Praz
dining_guide.apres_snacks: La Folie Douce (iconic music terrace), Le Tremplin (piste base), Bar des Pistes (Aman Le Mélézin)

piste_guide.best_for_beginners: Pralong area above Jardin Alpin, dedicated nursery zones near all villages
piste_guide.best_for_intermediates: Saulire-Creux upper sectors, Chanrossa above Moriond, long blues and reds
piste_guide.best_for_advanced: Grand Couloir (marked black couloir), steep mogul pistes under Saulire, off-piste in Bel Aire area
piste_guide.off_piste: Col du Fruit, Vallée des Avals (guide essential), Grand Couloir area, Bel Aire tree runs
piste_guide.crowding: Verdons/Jardin Alpin area gets very busy. Early starts recommended.
piste_guide.snowpark: 1 snowpark in Verdons area. Major parks on Méribel side (Le Park, Moon Park)

apres_guide.iconic: La Folie Douce — live music, dancing on tables, starts 2pm slope-side
apres_guide.bars: Le Tremplin (piste base), La Cave des Creux (terrace), Les Caves (nightclub), piano bars in luxury hotels
apres_guide.note: Polarised — ultra-luxury slope-side venues vs relaxed pubs. Something for both crowds.

honest_drawbacks: Expensive — 1850 is one of the most expensive resorts in the Alps
Purpose-built 1970s architecture under the luxury veneer — some areas are dated concrete
Verdons/Jardin Alpin area gets uncomfortably busy
February school holidays are packed and prices spike
Vehicles are restricted — Altiport private jet traffic can be noisy
Lower villages (1300, 1550) need lifts to reach the main ski area

nearest_airports.note: Private jets only — short runway, famous challenging approach

by_train.eurostar: London to Moûtiers direct in winter (from £99 each way)
by_train.shuttle: Regular bus services from Moûtiers to all Courchevel villages

practical_info.ski_rental: Multiple shops in all villages — ski hire from ~€25/day
practical_info.supermarket: Forum Centre (1850), smaller shops in other villages
practical_info.medical: Medical centre in 1850, hospital in Moûtiers (25km)
practical_info.altiport_landing: Courchevel Altiport has one of the most challenging approaches in Europe — steep uphill landing strip
